title: Kavach (train protection system)
wikitext:
{{Short description|Indian railway safety technology}}
{{distinguish|Kavach (anti-missile system)}}
'''KAVACH''' ({{lit|Armour}}) is an [[India]]n [[automatic train protection]] (ATP) system indigenously developed by [[Research Design and Standards Organisation]] (RDSO) in collaboration with Medha Servo Drives, Kernex Microsystems and HBL Power Systems.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-03 |title=Explained: How Railways' Indigenous Anti-Collision System Kavach Can Prevent Train Accidents |url=https://www.indiatimes.com/explainers/news/indian-railways-indigenous-anti-collision-system-kavach-565956.html |access-date=2024-10-03 |website=Indiatimes |language=en-IN}}</ref><ref name="2022test onair">{{Cite web |date = 5 March 2022 |title = Indian Railways tested 'Kavach'- an indigenous Automatic Train Protection System |url = https://newsonair.com/2022/03/05/indian-railways-tested-kavach-an-indigenous-automatic-train-protection-system/ |access-date = 21 May 2022 |website = NewsOnAIR |language = en-US}}</ref> Initially it was known by the name '''Train Collision Avoidance System''' ('''TCAS''').<ref name="Indian ATP">{{Cite web |last=Kessell |first=Clive |date=2023-05-02 |title=Enhancing Safety An Indian ATP alternative |url=https://www.railengineer.co.uk/enhancing-safety-an-indian-atp-alternative/ |access-date=2024-08-09 |website=Rail Engineer |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Geetanath |first1=V. |title=Parliament Standing Committee concerned over slow roll out of 'Kavach' |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/parliament-standing-committee-concerned-over-slow-roll-out-of-kavach/article69146379.ece?cx_testId=81&cx_testVariant=cx_1&cx_artPos=2&cx_experienceId=EXPO56ZDYSGX&cx_experienceActionId=showRecommendationsX1R7QXU17VG227#cxrecs_s |work=[[The Hindu]] |date=28 January 2025 |language=en-IN}}</ref> Kavach was adopted by [[Ministry of Railways (India)|Ministry of Railways]] as the ''National ATP System'' in July 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 December 2023 |title=Kavach Deployed On 1465 Route Km & 139 Locomotives |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1983975 |website=Press Information Bureau}}</ref>

[[File:TCAS working graphical explanation.jpg|thumb|Kavach functioning shown through schematic diagram]]

Development of Kavach began in 2011 as an [[open architecture]] system. In 2014, field trials commenced. First field trial experiments on passenger trains was done in February 2016. Subsequently, Kavach received [[Safety integrity level|Safety Integrity Level]] (SIL-4) certification in 2019.<ref name="Indian ATP" /> It is being promoted as one of the cheapest ATP systems available worldwide.<ref name="Shri trial">{{Cite news |date=4 March 2022 |title=Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw inspects the trial of Kavach System |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1802968#:~:text=KAVACH%20is%20meant%20to%20provide,as%20per%20the%20speed%20restrictions |work=Press Information Bureau}}</ref>

The [[Union budget of India]] for the FY 2022-23 allocated funds for the rapid implementation of Kavach across 2,000 km of track, as well as sanctioning its implementation along 34,000 km track of the [[Golden Quadrilateral]] rail route, which is to be implemented by 2027–2028.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-07 |title=Indian Railways Kavach to boost safety! How this indigenous technology can prevent two trains from colliding |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/railways-indian-railways-kavach-to-boost-safety-how-this-indigenous-technology-can-prevent-two-trains-from-colliding-2452777/ |access-date=2024-08-09 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref>

==Overview==
Kavach incorporates several key characteristics of the [[European Train Control System]] (ETCS) as well as the Indian [[Anti-collision device|Anti-Collision Device]] (ACD); however, ETCS is wider in its scope, since Kavach is not intended to function as a replacement for traditional [[Lineside signal]]s. While ETCS requires a centralised trackside infrastructure, Kavach is distributed, permitting piece-meal deployments. Kavach is also not intended to have interoperability with other country's systems, unlike ETCS' rigorous cross-border interoperability requirements.<ref name="railing 2023">{{cite web |url = https://www.railengineer.co.uk/enhancing-safety-an-indian-atp-alternative/ |title = Enhancing Safety An Indian ATP alternative |publisher = railengineer.co.uk |first = Clive |last = Kessell |date = 2 May 2023}}</ref> These aspects make it cheaper than ETCS.<ref name="trains colliding">{{Cite web |date=2022-03-04 |title=Explained: Kavach, the Indian technology that can prevent two trains from colliding |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-kavach-the-indian-technology-that-can-prevent-two-trains-from-colliding-7801295/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220324074349/https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-kavach-the-indian-technology-that-can-prevent-two-trains-from-colliding-7801295/ |archive-date=24 March 2022 |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

To use Kavach, each train must be either built with compatible apparatus or to undergo a retrofit of such apparatus. The system consists of few core elements, out of which computer and UHF/GSM radio infrastructure (which consists of [[radio modem]]s and antennas) are fitted, both at stations and onboard the locomotives; remaining are the [[radio-frequency identification]] (RFID) tags, that are placed between the running rails; and onboard the locomotives, there are RFID readers to read those RFID tags placed on the tracks along with a [[Kavach (train protection system)#Brake Interface Unit (BIU)|Brake Interface Unit (BIU)]] to provide Kavach, the interface to control the locomotive's braking system.<ref name="railing 2023" />

Kavach uses many data inputs to ascertain the location and direction of the train. The timing data is confirmed by a GPS satellite link, while the location and direction are measured by an [[odometer]] that resets itself whenever the train passes over an RFID tag. Loco pilots are provided with information through a DMI screen; an [[event recorder]] is present to retain a record of all interactions. Specific data exchanged includes speed, direction, location, and identifiers (individual to train and tracks). Some of the track-fitted RFID tags are used for additional purposes, such as to communicate an upcoming signal, [[level crossing]], or the train's entry and exit from a Kavach-covered area.<ref name="railing 2023" />

All messaging between trains and the trackside infrastructure is handled through [[radio communication]]. The radio towers used by the Kavach for communication are installed alongside the tracks, aligned with the lineside signalling equipment and railway stations, and are deployed at a regular interval of 1–5 km, depending on the overall terrain.<ref name="trains colliding" /><ref name="hindu 2022">{{Cite news |last=Geetanath |first=V. |date=12 November 2021 |title=SCR to cover 630 km of network with 'Kavach' by March-end |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/scr-to-cover-630-km-of-network-with-kavach-by-march-end/article37481170.ece |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220429181730/https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Hyderabad/scr-to-cover-630-km-of-network-with-kavach-by-march-end/article37481170.ece |archive-date=29 April 2022 |access-date=21 May 2022 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> Kavach communicate with relevant [[signalling control]] stations, being interfaced with both [[electronic interlocking]] (EI) and [[Relay interlocking|route relay interlocking (RRI)]] systems, functioning in both [[Absolute block signalling|absolute]] and [[automatic block signaling]] sections to retrieve information on signal aspects, permitted speeds, movement authority, and any restrictions; these criteria are continuously and automatically checked against each train's reported criteria and presented to the loco pilot on the DMI screen. The [[GSM-R]] radio link is also used to send data to the [[#Network Monitoring System (NMS)|Network Monitoring System (NMS)]] to log all train movements, inputs, and fault messages. Appropriate fault teams are automatically contacted to address issues that arise in real time.<ref name="railing 2023"/>

The initial implementation of the system harnesses [[ultra high frequency]] (UHF) radio frequencies, while the [[LTE (telecommunication)|LTE-R]] based version of Kavach (Version 4.0) will soon be rolled out.<ref name="trains colliding" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Law |first=Abhishek |date=2024-02-23 |title=Railways to upgrade Kavach to LTE; formal rollout likely in 12-15 months |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/logistics/railways-to-upgrade-kavach-to-lte-formal-rollout-likely-in-12-15-months/article67877357.ece |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Law |first=Abhishek |date=2024-08-07 |title=Indian Railways to roll out Kavach 4.0 by March 2025 |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/logistics/indian-railways-to-roll-out-kavach-40-by-fy25-end/article68497755.ece |access-date=2024-08-13 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}}</ref> Also, work is underway to integrate Kavach with Traffic Management System (TMS), [[Electronic interlocking|Electronic Interlocking System]] (EIS).<ref name="railing 2023" />

== Functions ==
Primarily, Kavach works on the principle of continuous supervision of the movement authority, and is designed to maintain train speed within the specified limits. It can automatically apply brakes to slow down or to bring the train to a complete standstill, in case the loco pilot violates the speed restrictions or fails to act in time to prevent [[signal passed at danger]] (SPAD), thereby reducing the risks of collision in block sections and on running lines at stations. It displays upcoming signal aspects in the loco pilot's cab on the DMI screen; this feature aids in the operation of high-speed trains and assists loco pilots during low visibility weather conditions.<ref name="railing 2023" />

Additionally, Kavach offers a few non-signalling-based non-SIL features, such as providing protection from head-on, rear-end, and side collisions by estimating the length of the track that the train is occupying in a block section and identifying the track that the train is on. It can detect and stop the train in case of a rollback. It automatically blows the horn when approaching a [[level crossing]] and manual [[SOS]] function which would trigger emergency brakes of all nearby trains.

== Development ==
=== Origins ===
During the early twenty-first century, [[Indian Railways]] became increasingly interested in deploying [[automatic train protection]] (ATP) upon its existing mixed-traffic routes.<ref name="railing 2023"/> An extensive evaluation of internationally available systems, such as the [[European Train Control System]] (ETCS), was conducted; it was ultimately concluded that there was no existing off the shelf ATP system that fulfilled its requirements. These requirements included the prevention of instances of [[signal passed at danger]] (SPAD), collision prevention, in-cab signalling, automatic whistling at level crossings, intelligent real-time health monitoring, and to facilitate substantial speed and capacity increases for both freight and passenger operations.<ref name="railing 2023"/> A further key target to be pursued in part via the addition of ATP is the Indian Railways' ambition to achieve a zero accident rate.<ref name="hindu 2022" />

Instead of procuring and installing an existing system, a project to domestically develop a suitable ATP system was pursued by Indian Railways instead.<ref name="railing 2023"/> During 2011, work on what would become Kavach commenced; this project was originally titled as the ''Train Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)''.<ref name="railing 2023"/><ref name="indianexpress explained2022">{{Cite web |last = Dastidar |first = Avishek G |date = 5 March 2022 |title = Explained: Kavach, the Indian technology that can prevent two trains from colliding |url = https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-kavach-the-indian-technology-that-can-prevent-two-trains-from-colliding-7801295/ |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220324074349/https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-kavach-the-indian-technology-that-can-prevent-two-trains-from-colliding-7801295/ |archive-date = 24 March 2022 |access-date = 21 May 2022 |website = The Indian Express |language = en-IN}}</ref> An early [[proof of concept]] was produced in 2012 while a development order for the design and manufacture of the system was issued during the following year. It is an [[open architecture]] system, as there was an explicit requirement for it to be interoperable between multiple vendors unlike in the case of [[anti-collision device]] (ACD).<ref name="railing 2023"/>

During 2014, the deployment of an initial trial system along a 265 km section of line commenced, upon with the first real world evaluations of Kavach were performed.<ref name="railing 2023"/>

===Validation===
Between 2015 and 2017, field trials of the system were carried out.<ref name="railing 2023"/> Data and experiences gathered from these trials were used to refine the specification, which was formalised in March 2017.<ref name="deccan test2022" /> Final approval of the system was issued in 2019, permitting the training of railway employees on Kavach ahead of the formal rollout and commencement of operations.<ref name="railing 2023"/> Kavach has been subjected to tests performed by an [[Italy]] based independent safety assessor (ISA) [[:it:Italcertifer|ITALCERTIFER S.p.A.]] to validate its performance.<ref name="minister test">{{Cite web |last=PTI |title=Indigenous train collision protection system 'Kavach' to be tested with railway minister on board |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/india/indigenous-train-collision-protection-system-kavach-to-be-tested-with-railway-minister-on-board-1087679.html |access-date=2024-08-10 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref> The Stationary Kavach achieved [[mean time between failures]] (MTBF) of 60,000 hours, MTBF of Loco Kavach is 40,000 hours while the RFID Reader, Radio modems and GPS/GSM antennas have recorded MTBF of 100,000 hours; reportedly achieved an overall availability of 99.9% during testing.<ref name="trains colliding" /> Accordingly, it has been certified with [[Safety integrity level|Safety Integrity Level]] (SIL)-4 for compliance with the [[European Committee for Electrotechnical Standardization|CENELEC]]/ [[List of EN standards|EN standards]] as per ''EN 50126:1999'' (covering specification and demonstration of [[Reliability, availability, maintainability and safety|RAMS]]), ''EN 50128:2011'' (relating to software for railway control and protection systems), ''EN 50129:2003'' (concerning safety related electronic systems for signalling), ''EN 50159:2010'' (covering safety related communication in transmission systems) norms.<ref name="2022test onair" /><ref name="trains colliding" /><ref name="minister test" /><ref name="indianexpress.com">{{Cite web |date=2022-03-24 |title=Explained: Kavach, the Indian technology that can prevent two trains from colliding {{!}} Explained News, The Indian Express |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-kavach-the-indian-technology-that-can-prevent-two-trains-from-colliding-7801295/ |access-date=2024-08-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220324074349/https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-kavach-the-indian-technology-that-can-prevent-two-trains-from-colliding-7801295/ |archive-date=2022-03-24}}</ref>

=== Confirmatory trials ===

On 4 March 2022, a high-profile live demonstration of Kavach was conducted between Gullaguda and Chitgidda railway stations in [[Secunderabad railway division|Secunderabad Division]]. Indian Railway minister [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]] was travelling in one locomotive travelling in one direction, while Vinay Kumar Tripathi, chairman and CEO of Indian Railway was travelling in another locomotive on the opposite direction on the same track while Kavach was operational. It detected that both locomotives were on the same track and responded by automatically applying the brakes on both trains, thus averting an impending collision.<ref>{{cite web |url = https://www.livemint.com/news/indian-railways-watch-video-of-how-kavach-system-averts-collision-of-two-trains-11646463822831.html|title = Indian Railways: Watch video of how 'Kavach' averts collision of two speeding trains}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last = Ani {{!}} |title = Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw reviews manufacturing of Vande Bharat train coaches in Chennai |url = https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/railway-minister-ashwini-vaishnaw-reviews-manufacturing-of-vande-bharat-train-coaches-in-chennai/videoshow/91694505.cms |access-date = 21 May 2022 |website = The Economic Times |date = 20 May 2022 |language=en-IN}}</ref>

On 16 February 2024, another trial of the system was carried out in the [[Agra railway division|Agra Division]]. At 9:30 am, the trial commenced between Mathura and Palwal. Till 2 in the afternoon, the entire exercise was repeated in both up and down directions. The trial was done on an eight-car [[Vande Bharat (trainset)|Vande Bharat]] train. During the trial, the Vande Bharat was travelling at s speed of 160 kmph and the system could stop the train 10 m before the red signal without the loco pilot applying brakes. A similar test will soon be carried out with the 16-coach Vande Bharat.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-17 |title='Kavach' trial: Vande Bharat train, running at 160 kmph, stops automatically before a red signal! |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/railways-kavach-trial-vande-bharat-train-running-at-160-kmph-stops-automatically-before-a-red-signal-3396964/ |access-date=2024-02-17 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref>

In March 2024, [[Italy|Italian]] certification and inspection service provider {{ill|Italcertifer S.p.A.|italic=yes|it|Italcertifer}} conducted a four-day independent safety assessment trial of the Kavach system installed between Mathura and Palwal section in the Agra Division, under the supervision of Kush Gupta, Deputy Chief Signal and Telecommunication Engineer of [[North Central Railway zone|NCR]]. The assessment began on March 19 and concluded on March 23. Multiple trials were conducted using a special trial train consisting of a [[Indian locomotive class WAP-5|WAP-5]] locomotive and 10 [[LHB coach]]es at speeds ranging from 130 to 160 Kmph.<ref>{{Cite web |last=PTI |date=2024-04-05 |title=Italian safety certification firm assesses Kavach system installed in Agra Rail Division |url=https://theprint.in/india/italian-safety-certification-firm-assesses-kavach-system-installed-in-agra-rail-division/2029675/ |access-date=2024-08-10 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref>

In September 2024, a successful trial of KAVACH 4.0 was conducted for the first time between [[Kota, Rajasthan|Kota]] and [[Sawai Madhopur]] of [[Kota railway division|Kota Division]] in [[West Central Railway zone]], in the presence of the [[Minister of Railways (India)|Railway Minister]] [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]] onboard the locomotive cab. The train travelling at the speed of {{Convert|130|km/h|abbr=on}} stopped just before {{Convert|50|m|abbr=on}} before a red signal without human interference in the braking system. According to a railway official, “The train was running at 130 kmph and the moment it entered a section where there was a permanent speed restriction of 120 kmph, the Kavach brought down its speed to 120 and then after crossing it regained the 130 kmph speed.” The system has been tested for seven different emergency situations and has provided satisfactory results. In the following situation, the train entered a "loop" with a speed restriction of {{Convert|30|km/h|abbr=on}} and the Kavach successfully brought the speed down from {{Convert|130|km/h|abbr=on}} to the desired speed before entering the loop. During the other trials, the station master reported some kind of faults with the train when the Kavach system automatically applied its brakes to stop it, while in the other situation, the system applied the horns before a level crossing when the loco pilot failed to do so. The trial continued for half an hour.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-24 |title=Successful Kavach trial: Train stops 50 metres before red signal on its own – Know all test cases here |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/railways-successful-kavach-trial-train-stops-50-metres-before-red-signal-on-its-own-know-all-test-cases-here-3620888/#amp_tf=From%20%251$s&aoh=17272507119097&csi=0&referrer=https://www.google.com&ampshare=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/railways-successful-kavach-trial-train-stops-50-metres-before-red-signal-on-its-own-know-all-test-cases-here-3620888/ |access-date=2024-09-25 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref><ref name="covered 5-6" />

== System architecture ==
[[File:TCAS information flowchart.jpg|thumb|center|Flowchart illustrating the exchange of data between various components of KAVACH (grey) and other signalling equipment (blue)]]

=== Trackside and stationary components ===
====RFID tags====
[[File:TCAS RFID Tag.jpg|thumb|RFID tags clamped on the track sleeper near a level crossing]]

[[Radio-frequency identification|RFID]] Tags are fastened to the track sleepers at predetermined intervals. It contains pre-programmed data and a distinct track identification number (TIN). The RFID Tag transfers track information and precise location data to the onboard KAVACH computer when a locomotive passes over them and is scanned by the locomotive's RFID readers.

====Stationary Master Computer====
[[File:TCAS Stationary Master Computer.jpg|thumb|KAVACH Master Computer]]

The stationary Master Computer consists of a Vital Computer (electronic modules) and radio modems.

=====Vital Computer=====

The Vital Computer is the heart of stationary KAVACH units. It consists of a number of electronic modules with software that performs all the tasks. It receives information from signalling and interlocking systems and generates messages that are relayed to the locomotive by the radio unit in real-time.

=====Radio unit and antennas=====
[[File:TCAS Station UHF Radio Tower.jpg|thumb|KAVACH station radio tower]]

KAVACH's radio unit consists of two duplex [[Ultra high frequency|UHF]] radio modems having separate pair of [[Transmitter|Tx]]/[[Radio receiver|Rx]] [[MIMO]] antennas. Radio modems have a channel bandwidth of 25 KHz and a working frequency range of 406–470 MHz. It uses [[Time-division multiple access|TDMA]] and [[Frequency-division multiple access|FDMA]] radio communication protocols to connect with the locomotive's onboard KAVACH unit.

====Remote Interface Unit (RIU)====
[[File:TCAS RIU.jpg|thumb|KAVACH Remote Interface Unit (RIU)]]

RIU is identical to the stationary master computer, without the radio unit. It is used for retrieving remote signalling functions like from the end cabins, distributed interlocking systems, level crossings, and intermediate block sections coming within the coverage area of the station's radio tower. It relays information and exchanges data with the stationary master computer over [[Fiber-optic cable|fibre-optic cables]] ([[dark fibre]]).

====Station Master Operation Cum Indication Panel (SMOCIP)====
[[File:TCAS SMOCIP.jpg|thumb|KAVACH SM-OCIP Unit]]

SMOCIP is installed on the station master's desk and features an LCD for reading messages, an analog SOS counter and buttons for generating [[SOS]] and acknowledging messages. It requires a physical key to operate to avoid undesired and accidental operation of buttons.

=== Locomotive on-board components ===
====RFID reader====
[[File:TCAS RFID Reader P7.jpg|thumb|RFID reader mounted under a [[Indian locomotive class WAP-7|WAP-7]] locomotive]]

A locomotive fitted with KAVACH has two RFID readers mounted under its underframe. It scans the RFID tags attached to the track and transmits the information to the onboard KAVACH computer for processing.

====Onboard radio unit and antennas====
[[File:TCAS loco antennas.png|thumb|Two pairs of UHF Tx/Rx antennas (black) along with GSM and GPS antennas (red) on [[Vande Bharat (trainset)|Vande Bharat trainset]]]]

The onboard radio unit is similar to that of the stationary KAVACH radio unit.

Along with the two pairs of Tx/Rx UHF [[MIMO]] antennas, an additional [[GSM]]/[[General Packet Radio Service|GPRS]] and [[Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System|GPS]]/[[Satellite navigation|GNSS]] antenna are fitted on the locomotive.

KAVACH uses [[GSM-R]] network (as of version 3.2) for communicating fault messages to [[Kavach (train protection system)#Network Monitoring System (NMS)|Network Monitoring System (NMS)]] and for transferring authentication keys with the Stationary TCAS unit as well as with any nearby Loco TCAS units.

Both [[Global Positioning System|GPS]] and [[Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System|NavIC]] are used for updating live location of the locomotive and also for synchronizing [[Global Positioning System#Timekeeping|GPS Time]] with the [[Real-time clock|CPU Time]] of onboard KAVACH Computer.

====Onboard KAVACH computer====

[[File:TCAS Loco Computer.jpg|thumb|KAVACH locomotive onboard computer]]
Onboard computer is the main data processing centre of KAVACH system. It supervises the movement of the train by exchanging and synchronizing information collected from other onboard equipment, stationary KAVACH units and as well as from other nearby KAVACH equipped locomotives.

DMI, also known as the Loco Pilot-Operation Cum Indication Panel (LP-OCIP), consists of a colour [[TFT LCD|TFT]] touchscreen display and buttons. It uses audio-visuals to display warnings and information. It features a [[SOS]] and an acknowledgement button for use of loco pilots.

====Brake Interface Unit (BIU)====

BIU provides KAVACH with an interface to the locomotive's braking system and monitors its overall health. It prioritises the highest brake demand between the one initiated manually by the loco pilots and the one initiated by the KAVACH and applies brakes accordingly.

===Other components===
====Network Monitoring System (NMS)====
[[File:TCAS - NMS Server.jpg|thumb|Network Monitoring System server of Kavach]]

NMS over the [[Fibre optic network|OFC network]] (E1 interface) centralises monitoring of Kavach-equipped trains and stations. It handles [[Troubleshooting|Error Troubleshooting]], offline simulation and [[Real-time computing|Real-time monitoring]] of Loco-Kavach. Both Stationary and Loco-Kavach send fault messages to the NMS; while Loco-Kavach units are exclusively connected to NMS through the [[GSM-R]] link; stationary Kavach units are connected through both [[Ethernet]] ([[Fiber-optic cable|OFC cables]]) and the GSM-R link. A central server in the Division Control Room logs all relayed information and radio packets exchanged between stations and locomotives, which are made accessible through the NMS.

====Key Management System (KMS)====
KMS is a server that shares secret [[Authenticated Key Exchange|Authentication Keys]] with Stationary and Loco-Kavach units to ensure message integrity and authenticity during [[Radio communication]]. These keys protect messages from modification and impersonation and are shared after authenticating the Loco-Kavach through [[One-time password]]. KMS is deployed on a secure internet server, and Loco-Kavach units periodically request these keys for radio communication. [[GSM-R]] modules in the [[Train event recorder]] connects Loco-Kavach to [[General Packet Radio Service|GPRS]]. KMS uses [[Aes-128|AES-128]] encryption for communication between Stationary and Loco-Kavach units and transfers keys through GSM-R. A central KMS server at headquarters manages key distribution, with all Kavach IDs and [[SIM card|SIM]] numbers provided to [[RailTel]] for updates. Communication is currently on [[General Packet Radio Service|GPRS]] but will shift to [[LTE (telecommunication)|LTE-R]] with Kavach-4.0.

====Temporary Speed Restriction Management System (TSRMS)====
TSRMS is newly introduced on Kavach-4.0. It is a dedicated server used for feeding temporary speed restrictions to the track profile data packet. Like that of [[Kavach (train protection system)#Network Monitoring System (NMS)|NMS]], each Stationary-Kavach unit is also connected to the TSRMS [[Fibre optic network|OFC network]] through its own dedicated E1 interface. The network uses the [[Ethernet]] protocol to exchange data packets between Stationary-Kavach units and the TSRMS server and uses [[LTE (telecommunication)|LTE-R]] for [[Authenticated Key Exchange]] with Loco-Kavach.

== Commissioning ==
On July 30, 2025, Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the successful implementation of Kavach 4.0, safety system, on the Mathura-Kota stretch of the busy Delhi-Mumbai corridor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Shivam |date=2025-08-02 |title=Indigenous Kavach 4.0 Safety System Commissioned on This Section of Indian Railways |url=https://currentaffairs.adda247.com/indigenous-kavach-4-0-safety-system-commissioned-on-this-section-of-indian-railways/ |access-date=2025-08-03 |website=adda247 |language=en-IN}}</ref> Train speeds are set to increase beyond current limits once the testing phase is successfully completed.

== Training of personnel ==
The railway minister stated that Kavach 4.0 is expected to be deployed across the entire country within the next six years.{{when|date=July 2026}} To facilitate this large-scale implementation:<ref name=":0" />

* More than 30,000 railway staff members have already received training on the Kavach system.
* [[Indian Railways Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications|IRISET]] (Indian Railway Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications) has partnered with 17 AICTE-accredited engineering colleges, universities, and institutions through MoUs to integrate Kavach technology into B.Tech programs, helping build a future-ready talent pool.

== Deployment ==

=== Cost of installation ===

Kavach is one of the least expensive ATP systems in the world. The cost of installing it on the tracks, including equipment, is {{INRConvert|50|l}} per route kilometre and {{INRConvert|70|l}} to fit the equipment in one locomotive.<ref name="Shri trial" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-25 |title=Kavach question: Will Budget hike for Railways help prevent train accidents? |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/railways-budget-2024-kavach-installation-safety-train-accidents-2571691-2024-07-25 |access-date=2024-08-10 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref><ref name="indianexpress.com"/>

=== Manufacturers ===

The [[Original equipment manufacturer|Original Equipment Manufacturers]] (OEMs) that are manufacturing the Kavach equipment includes Medha Servo Drives, HBL Power Systems, and Kernex Microsystems. Other firms that have been vying for the approval to be vendors include GGTronic', Quadrant Future Tek, Areca Embedded Systems, Lotus Wireless Technologies and the state-owned [[Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited|BHEL]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-11 |title=Why railway safety remains on slow track |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india-today-insight/story/why-railway-safety-remains-on-slow-track-2565428-2024-07-11 |access-date=2024-08-10 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=Lotus Wireless Technologies India Private Limited | date=2014-07-26 | url=https://www.careratings.com/upload/CompanyFiles/PR/202407130723_Lotus_Wireless_Technologies_India_Private_Limited.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240810220848/https://www.careratings.com/upload/CompanyFiles/PR/202407130723_Lotus_Wireless_Technologies_India_Private_Limited.pdf | archive-date=2024-08-10}}</ref> [[Multinational corporation|MNCs]] like [[Japan]]'s KYOSAN and [[Germany]]'s [[Siemens]] are also working on Kavach.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-11-30 |title=In a first, Indian Railways allows MNCs to deploy indigenous Kavach anti train collision system on network |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/in-a-a-first-indian-railways-allows-mncs-to-deploy-indigenous-kavach-anti-train-collision-system-on-network/articleshow/105611337.cms |access-date=2024-08-03 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

* 1,456 km or 3% of the entire rail network along with 144 locomotives of [[South Central Railway zone|South Central Railway]] is equipped with Kavach.
* From FY2025-26 onwards, Kavach will be implemented on 5,000-5,500 km of the network per year.
* As for the locomotives, the rollout of the system is planned in multiple phases.
** In the first phase, tender will be released for equipping 10,000 (50%) locomotives with Kavach. The cost of Kavach per locomotive is around {{INR convert|72|l|lk=on}} which translates to approximately {{INR convert|7200|c|lk=on}} project for the first phase. The tender for first phase is planned to be closed by October 2024. This phase will also include equipping 9,000 Route kms of network with Kavach 4.0 version. The sanction for first phase has been secured. 
** The second phase will incorporate the system for the rest of 10,000 locomotives. The newly built [[Indian locomotive class WAG-9|WAG-9HH]] locomotives and [[Vande Bharat (trainset)|Vande Bharat trainsets]] will be equipped with Kavach 4.0 apparatus.
* The survey work for 8,000 stations is to be completed by December 2024. It will take four years to equip the entire inventory of locomotives with Kavach. As for the routes, [[New Delhi–Mumbai main line]] and [[Howrah–Delhi main line]] will be covered initially which measures 3,000 km. This will be followed by [[New Delhi–Chennai main line|Delhi – Chennai]] and [[Mumbai–Chennai line|Mumbai – Chennai]] routes covering 3,300 km. Subsequently, this will be increased to all automatic signalling sections of 5,000 Rkm.

The tender for the first phase of implementation, worth {{INR convert|7200|c|lk=on}}, is to be released on 19 September 2024.<ref name="open 9-19" />

On August 12, 2025, West Central Railway awarded HBL Power Systems a contract of {{INRConvert|54.12|c|lk=on}} to install Kavach in the 166 km Kota-Ruthiyai segment and the Sogaria-Kota "C" section. extract:
KAVACH (lit. 'Armour') is an Indian automatic train protection (ATP) system indigenously developed by Research Design and Standards Organisation (RDSO) in collaboration with Medha Servo Drives, Kernex Microsystems and HBL Power Systems. Initially it was known by the name Train Collision Avoidance System (TCAS). Kavach was adopted by Ministry of Railways as the National ATP System in July 2020.

Development of Kavach began in 2011 as an open architecture system. In 2014, field trials commenced. First field trial experiments on passenger trains was done in February 2016. Subsequently, Kavach received Safety Integrity Level (SIL-4) certification in 2019. It is being promoted as one of the cheapest ATP systems available worldwide.
The Union budget of India for the FY 2022-23 allocated funds for the rapid implementation of Kavach across 2,000 km of track, as well as sanctioning its implementation along 34,000 km track of the Golden Quadrilateral rail route, which is to be implemented by 2027–2028.
